summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the fourth type of ghusl (ritual bathing) that is preferred in Islamic jurisprudence: bathing after burying a disbeliever. This is an extremely rare and obscure scenario that occurs only when a Muslim is directly responsible for physically burying a non-Muslim relative due to the absence of other family members or community members willing to perform this duty. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses the historical example of Ali ibn Abi Talib burying his father Abu Talib to illustrate this principle, while clarifying the strict Islamic guidelines that prohibit Muslims from attending non-Muslim funerals, making dua for disbelievers, or performing full funeral rites for them. He emphasizes that this situation is so rare it is virtually impossible for most Muslims to encounter, but scholars mention it for completeness and historical reference.
